Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons for pilot — pricing detail request

Laura —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our Platform team liked the visualization suite and the KV/prefix retention ideas for reducing cold-start cost. Before we loop procurement I need a clearer commercial picture so I can model TCO for Q3:

- A compact price for the Advanced Dashboards (seat-based) vs a metered visualization SKU (per-ingest).
- Retention tier pricing for traces and full-text logs (30/90/365 days).
- Any pilot credits you can extend and whether commit dollars for Hosted inference can be amortized against add-on fees.

Procurement wants to see a single-line commitment option (annual) with a known monthly amortization schedule and a retention SLA for 365-day tier. They also requested a sample SOW and a pricing spreadsheet.

Can you share options by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering
Stella Health
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached are two artifacts: a short SOW (SOW_Stella-visual-pack.pdf) and a pricing model (pricing-model-stella.xlsx) that outline the three packaging options. High-level answers inline below, followed by next steps.

- Dashboards: 1) seat-based Core Dashboards (per-seat/month) 2) Metered Visuals (per-ingest USD) 3) Hybrid (base seats + metered overage). We included example breakpoints so you can see where hybrid starts to win.
- Retention (traces/logs): Tiered rates for 30/90/365. We propose a retention floor for large commits to guarantee a minimum allocation of GB-months at reduced unit pricing; floor amount is negotiable with commit level.
- Pilot credits: We can offer a $25k pilot credit against the first 90 days of add-on consumption for a 12-month commit >= $300k. Pilot credit is applied as a one-time invoice credit (not a refund).
- Amortization: We can amortize an annual Hosted inference commit across add-ons on a monthly basis for billing clarity. This requires contract language mapping the commit to a pre-paid credit pool in the order form.
- SLA: For the 365-day archival tier we can commit to durability/availability objectives and a 30-day data-recovery RTO in the SOW; anything stricter becomes an enterprise SLA add-on.

I've proposed three commercial options in sheet tab 'Compact/Hybrid/Committed' and put a sample annual amortization schedule in the 'Amortization' tab.

Next steps: If procurement likes one of the options I can prepare a term sheet and a DocuSign-ready order form. Ben, can you confirm if we can make the amortization language standard or if we need legal review?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_Stella-visual-pack.pdf (pdf), pricing-model-stella.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons for pilot — pricing detail request

Laura — quick thoughts for the pricing model before we share with procurement: 

- Hybrid product framing: emphasize base seats cover dashboards/UX while metered credits handle spikes (helps Stella avoid large overprovisioning). Give them an example: 50 seats + 1TB/month metered = $X/mo vs 200 seats fixed = $Y/mo.
- Retention floor: suggest we tier floors by commit band (e.g., $300k, $600k, $1.2M) and pre-allocate a retention pool (GB-months) that draws down before metered charges apply. That phrasing keeps billing simple.
- Discounting: sales-compression to procurement: up to 18% on add-ons at $600k+ commit; for $300k commit cap at 12%. If procurement asks 20% we can offer a one-time onboarding credit to bridge the gap instead of increasing discount.
- Paperwork: we should include a clause that amortization credits are non-transferable and expire 12 months after contract start. That protects revenue recognition.

I'll take the pricing-model and add a simple 'comparable-configs' tab that maps to their usage patterns. Karthik, flag anything on billing/legal that blocks amortization as structured.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Laura / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the model. Procurement has a few follow-ups after reviewing:

1) They want the 12-month commit to be presented as a single-line dollar commitment with a defined monthly amortization to apply against both Hosted inference and the Visual Pack add-ons.
2) Discount: internal ask is 20% on add-ons at the $300k commit level. If you cannot do 20% they'd accept 12% + a $10k onboarding credit.
3) Retention SLA: procurement would like a 99.95% availability target for archival retrieval and an RTO of 14 days for the 365-day tier. They say this is standard for healthcare partners.
4) Approval path: they require DocuSign-ready order form and a PO within 10 business days after sign.

Can you confirm we can get a DocuSign link and a clean term sheet (no redlines) by EOD tomorrow? We'll prepare the PO once the DocuSign is live.

Marta

Marta —

We can accommodate most of your requests. Quick confirmations:

- DocuSign & term sheet: yes — I will send a DocuSign-ready order form and a one-page term sheet by EOD (link prep in progress).
- Pricing: we can accept a 12% add-on discount at $300k commit + a $10k onboarding credit (applied as one-time invoice credit). To reach 20% at that band we'd need to move to the $600k commit tier.
- Amortization: we can structure the annual commit as a prepaid credit pool with a monthly amortization schedule that applies to Hosted inference and add-ons. We'll include the non-transferable/12-month-expiry language Ben suggested.
- Retention SLA: 99.95% is fine for availability; RTO 14 days for the 365-day tier is acceptable provided we include an exception for disaster-recovery scenarios in the SOW. For stricter RTOs we can build an enterprise add-on.

I'll circulate the signed-ready docs and the DocuSign link (https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef123456) once legal approves the final language. Karthik — please review the contract language for amortization and the non-transferable clause; flag anything that will slow approval.

Once sign is complete we will apply the $25k pilot credit (per the initial offer) and the $10k onboarding credit at invoice.

Thanks — talk soon,
